decoys.text: Keep watch today: who is acting oddly?
Notice who changes the subject quickly whenever suspicion comes up in conversation before the next vote.
Watch who moves around the most before the next vote, and ask yourself why.
Keep track of who sits where at the next gathering, and whether anyone has moved.
Listen for anyone who repeats an unusual word or phrase before the next vote.
Count how many times each person laughs during the next conversation. Who seems forced?
Pay attention to who asks the most questions during the next conversation.
Notice who agrees with everyone. Agreeing with everything can be a way to hide.
Watch for anyone fiddling with something in their hand.
Notice who steers conversations onto unexpected topics before the next vote.
Look out for anyone who seems to be waiting for someone else to say something specific.
Keep an eye on the things around you. Has anything moved since the last vote?
Watch who pays the most compliments. Flattery can be a cover.
Notice who is quickest to accuse someone, and who is slowest.
Remember who voted for whom last time, and see whether anyone's story about their vote changes before the next vote.
Watch who goes quiet when the conversation turns to suspicion.
Pick one person and watch them closely until the next vote. Are they behaving the way they usually do?
Listen for anyone telling an oddly specific story, and ask yourself why they chose those details.
Notice who keeps offering to help others today. Kindness is lovely, but could it also be a cover?
Watch for pairs of people who seem to avoid each other.
Keep watch: who seems to be ticking something off a mental list?
Notice who checks their phone most often.
Watch whether anyone quietly tries to get other people to swap seats or move around before the next vote.
Decide who has been least suspected so far, and watch them closely before the vote.
Listen out for anyone using the same phrase twice. It may mean nothing, or a great deal.
Notice who starts group activities before the next vote. Leading can be a way of steering people.
Watch who asks questions they already seem to know the answers to.
Keep a quiet note of anyone who mentions the weather, food or holidays more than once.
Notice anyone trying very hard to make others laugh during the next conversation.
Watch who seems most relaxed in conversation. Calm can be confidence, or rehearsal.
Notice anyone whose behaviour changes suddenly.
Watch who leaps to defend the most suspected player. Is it loyalty, or a plan?
Count how many different people each player talks to before the next vote. Who is spreading themselves most widely?
Look for anyone holding something they did not have earlier in the day, and ask yourself where it came from and why.
Notice who is always in the middle of conversations, and who stays at the edges.
Watch who keeps returning to the same topic, however unrelated.
Notice anyone asking others lots of questions about their past, such as first jobs, first gigs or first cars.
Keep watch today: who seems pleased with themselves for no obvious reason at all?
Note who suggests photos, games or activities. Is there a purpose behind it?
Watch who repeats what others have just said, word for word.
Listen for odd words dropped into conversation, such as a fruit or an animal from nowhere.
Notice who seems to be counting something on their fingers or under their breath during the day.
Before the next vote, decide who you trust most, then watch closely whether they really earn it.
Watch whether anyone tries to get the whole group doing the same thing at exactly the same moment today.
Notice who sings, hums or whistles today. Is it just a habit, or something else?
Notice who is teaching others games or tricks today.
